text:
sarah: FYI customer on prod (dedicated) reports Python streaming generator just hangs when an SSE event is split across TCP chunks. They see the HTTP stream keep-alive but our generator never yields the final tokens.

mike_dev: Can you paste the minimal repro + SDK + python versions? Also any request library (httpx/requests) details.

sarah: Using redwood-python-sdk 0.9.2, python 3.10, httpx 0.24.3. Code is a tiny loop:```python
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.getenv('RW_KEY'))
gen = client.responses.stream(model='gpt-3.5', input='hello')
for token in gen:
    print(token, end='')
```
We reproduced by writing a tiny server that sends `data:` lines split mid-json and with small sleeps. Client output never resumes until connection closed.

mike_dev: Any logs from the network capture? SSE events should end with a blank line (\n\n). If the server splits that across chunks the parser should still accumulate. Is it stuck accumulating?

sarah: Here's a short log from tcpdump + our client debug:```
< chunk 1 > 'data: {"text": "Hello'
< chunk 2 > ' world"}\n\n'
client DBG: sse_parser.buffer='data: {"text": "Hello'
client DBG: waiting for event terminator...
// then next chunk arrives
client DBG: sse_parser.buffer now complete but generator does not yield
```
We've confirmed the buffer contains full event but the generator coroutine stays blocked. Happens reproducibly when keepalive/retry middleware is enabled.

ryan_ml: Hm. That suggests a race between retry logic and parser state machine. If a retry wraps the response iterator and replaces the underlying stream object, we could lose the notify that new data arrived, or the generator future isn't scheduled. Did you test with retries disabled?

sarah: With retries off it mostly works — yields as expected. With exponential backoff enabled (defaults) the hang appears ~1/10 runs. Also observed a variant where a 401 comes back mid-stream (token rotation), client does an auth-refresh and replays a request which causes the generator to expect a different stream id.

mike_dev: Can you share a minimal server to repro? I'll try to reproduce locally.

sarah: Minimal repro server (python):```python
import socket, time
MSG1 = b"data: {\"text\": \"Hello"
MSG2 = b" world\"}\n\n"

s = socket.socket(); s.bind(('127.0.0.1', 9001)); s.listen(1);
conn, _ = s.accept();
conn.send(b"HTTP/1.1 200 OK\r\nContent-Type: text/event-stream\r\n\r\n")
conn.send(MSG1); time.sleep(0.15); conn.send(MSG2); time.sleep(0.5); conn.close()
```
Client hangs in loop on the same machine ~80% of runs when backed by httpx with keepalive pooling.

ryan_ml: Sounds like two issues colliding: 1) retry/auth refresh that swaps stream objects without flushing parser, and 2) parser not flushing on connection close. Quick mitigation: upgrade to 0.9.4 (we patched a flush-on-close bug there) or disable automatic retries for streaming calls. Also you can set `client._transport.max_keepalive=0` temporarily to avoid connection pooling triggering the race.

sarah: Verified: upgrading local bundle to 0.9.4 fixes the hang in our simple repro. Workaround for customer: pin to 0.9.4 or disable retries on streaming endpoints. Customer is on pinned 0.9.2, we recommended 0.9.4.

mike_dev: Can you open an internal issue with repro and the race details? I'll attach a proposed patch to flush parser buffer on socket close and ensure generator future is scheduled if buffer non-empty.

support-bot: Created ticket S-1234: "python-sse-stream-generator-hang-on-split-chunk" and linked customer case CASE-8765.

sarah: Also note we saw one customer report where a 401 during stream led to token refresh try that returned a short 204 and our retry logic swallowed the final blank line — another variant that can cause hang. Will include in repro.

ryan_ml: Plan: (1) backport flush-on-close fix to 0.9.3 patch release if customer needs fast upgrade (2) add extra integration test that splits SSE events across TCP boundaries + retries on/off (3) add a library option `streaming_retries=False` that disables retry wrapper for streaming calls by default in next major.

mike_dev: Sounds good. For the customer immediate workaround, we told them: upgrade to 0.9.4 OR set `client.responses.stream(retries=0)` and we will follow up with a patch. :thumbsup: 

support-bot: Customer notified via CASE-8765.

mike_dev: I'll post PR soon with tests. Thanks for the clear repro, Sarah.
